title: How does a picture of dots grow, three, six, nine?
description: The numbers three, six and nine are drawn as columns of dots. The video shows that each picture adds a whole column of three dots, and Keeko's doubt, that each picture adds one dot, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: a picture of a sequence grows by the same piece each time, and that piece is the jump. Watch for students who think a growing picture adds one dot at a time.

source: Draw the first three pictures of the sequence 3, 6, 9 with d
video_script.why: The child draws a sequence as dot pictures and sees that the jump is the piece that each new picture adds.
video_script.substitution: A picture grows by the same piece each time, and that piece is the jump.
video_script.anchor: three frames in a row for pictures 1, 2 and 3, with the numbers 3, 6, 9 under them
video_script.wrong_answer: each picture adds one more dot
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says each picture adds one more dot, because the pictures keep growing. Picture one has three dots and picture two has six, so three dots were added, and the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Each picture adds a column of three dots

final_answer.value: Each picture adds a column of 3 dots
final_answer.spoken: each picture adds a column of three dots

hold_back: Each picture adds a column of 3 dots
never_show: each picture adds one more dot
maths_rules: picture 1: one column of 3 dots, 3 dots in all
picture 2: two columns of 3 dots, 6 dots in all
picture 3: three columns of 3 dots, 9 dots in all
the picture grows by a column of 3 dots, which is the jump of the sequence
video_script.design: One idea: the picture grows by the same piece each time. Assumes finding a jump. Wrong idea: each picture adds one dot. The three frames stay on the board to the end.

<bookmark mark='frames'/>The numbers are three, six and nine, and each gets a picture made of dots.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How does the picture grow from one frame to the next?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.dots: three dots appear one above the other
marks.num: the number three is written beside them

narration: <bookmark mark='dots'/>We can show a number as dots, with the dots drawn in a neat shape.
<bookmark mark='num'/>Dots one above the other make a column, and counting the dots gives back the number.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers three, six and nine.

beats.on_screen: To find: the three pictures, and how the picture grows

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>Step one, picture one. Draw one column of three dots, so there are three dots in all.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, picture 2: two columns of 3 dots, 6 dots in all

marks.p2: a second column of three dots appears beside the first, in the second frame

narration: <bookmark mark='p2'/>Step two, picture two. Draw a second column of three dots next to the first. Two columns of three dots make six dots.

marks.p3: a third column of three dots appears in the third frame

narration: <bookmark mark='p3'/>Step three, picture three. Draw a third column in the same way. Three columns of three dots make nine dots.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Each picture adds a column of 3 dots

marks.ans: the answer is boxed and the new column of each picture is outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each picture adds a column of three dots, and three is the jump of the sequence.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble; picture 1 and picture 2 side by side, the new column outlined with 3 dots; the bubble is struck through

marks.count: the new column in picture two is outlined and its three dots are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks each picture adds one more dot, because the pictures keep growing.
<bookmark mark='count'/>But picture one has three dots and picture two has six dots.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Three new dots were added, which is one whole column and not a single dot.
